note: validateRegistration(d) returns { registrationClass, deadlineStatus, daysSinceConfirmation, informantQualified, blockingRules } and detectFlaggedIssues(state) returns the flags, so this is a SPLIT engine: the oracle pins detectFlaggedIssues(state) as expected.flaggedIssues with flagsArgs ["state"], mirroring form-app.js. There is no wall-clock dependence: the 5-day clock counts from medical.medicalExaminerConfirmationDate to registration.registrationDate (or to registration.asOfDate while unregistered), so the 'timestamp' key added by form-app.js is the only time-varying output. Classification is first-match: coroner referred and no coroner certificate -> 'referred-to-coroner-pending'; any blocking rule -> 'incomplete'; registrationDate set -> 'registered'; else 'ready-to-register'. Deadline: more than 5 days -> overdue (or registered-late), 4 or 5 days -> due-soon. Regenerate expected with: bin/test-personas united-kingdom-death-registration --update

personas.name: Ready to register, on track
personas.description: Expected hospital death; medical examiner confirmed 2026-09-01, assessed 2026-09-02 (1 day elapsed); not a coroner case; son present at the death is a qualified informant; appointment booked, documents to hand, cremation planned, five copies to be bought at registration. Expect ready-to-register, on-track, and no flags.

personas.name: Ready but due soon, loose ends
personas.description: Confirmed 2026-08-30, assessed 2026-09-03: 4 of 5 days used so the deadline is due-soon. No appointment booked, no documents to hand, disposal undecided, no copies planned. Expect ready-to-register, due-soon, with due-soon, appointment, documents, disposal-undecided and copies flags.

flaggedIssues.description: 4 of the 5 days allowed since the medical examiner’s confirmation have passed.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Register now; if more time is needed tell the register office immediately.

flaggedIssues.description: No registration appointment is booked.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Book an appointment with the register office for the district where the death occurred.

flaggedIssues.description: Supporting documents are not to hand. They are helpful but not mandatory.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Take what is available: the deceased’s birth or marriage certificate, passport, NHS medical card, driving licence, and proof of address.

flaggedIssues.description: The method of disposal has not been decided.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Decide between burial and cremation with the funeral director; cremation needs further forms.

flaggedIssues.description: No certified copies of the death certificate are planned. Banks, insurers and probate usually each need one.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Decide how many copies are needed; copies are cheaper bought at registration than ordered later.

personas.name: Ready but overdue
personas.description: Confirmed 2026-08-25 and still unregistered on 2026-09-03: 9 days, past the 5-day limit. The informant cannot give all of the deceased's particulars. Expect ready-to-register, overdue, with overdue and particulars flags.

flaggedIssues.description: The death must be registered within 5 days of the medical examiner’s confirmation, and 9 days have passed.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Tell the register office immediately and book the earliest appointment; weekends and bank holidays count towards the deadline.

flaggedIssues.description: The informant cannot give the deceased’s full particulars (names, birth date and place, last address, occupation, marital status).
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Gather the particulars from a relative or the deceased’s documents before the appointment.

personas.name: Registered in time, complete
personas.description: Confirmed 2026-08-29 and registered 2026-09-01 (3 days). Burial certificate issued, Tell Us Once reference received, three copies ordered online with a GRO index reference and priority service. Expect registered, registered-in-time, and no flags.

personas.name: Registered late, loose ends
personas.description: Confirmed 2026-08-20 and registered 2026-08-30 (10 days, late). The burial certificate has not been issued, no Tell Us Once reference was recorded, and two copies are to be ordered online without a GRO index reference. Expect registered, registered-late, with late-registration, disposal-certificate, Tell Us Once and GRO index flags.

flaggedIssues.description: The death was registered 10 days after the medical examiner’s confirmation, later than the 5-day limit.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: No action on this registration; note the delay for the record.

flaggedIssues.description: The certificate for burial or cremation (the green form) has not been issued, and the funeral cannot take place without it.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Ask the registrar for the green form and give it to the funeral director, crematorium or burial authority.

flaggedIssues.description: No Tell Us Once reference number is recorded.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Ask the registrar for the Tell Us Once reference number so government departments can be informed in one go.

flaggedIssues.description: No GRO index reference is recorded: ordering online without it adds a search fee and takes about 15 working days.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Find the GRO index reference (the register office can supply it) to avoid the extra fee.

personas.name: Referred to coroner, pending
personas.description: The death was reported to a coroner, an inquest has been opened and the coroner's certificate has not arrived. Registration waits and the clock is paused. Priority service is requested by post (not available). Expect referred-to-coroner-pending, paused-coroner, with coroner-pending, copies and priority flags.

flaggedIssues.description: The death has been reported to a coroner and the coroner’s certificate has not been received. The death cannot be registered yet.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Wait for the coroner to send the certificate (form CN2, or the certificate after inquest) to the registrar; ask the coroner for an interim certificate if proof of death is needed meanwhile.

flaggedIssues.description: No certified copies of the death certificate are planned. Banks, insurers and probate usually each need one.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Decide how many copies are needed; copies are cheaper bought at registration than ordered later.

flaggedIssues.description: The priority (next working day) service is only available when ordering online from the General Register Office.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Order online from the GRO, or drop the priority request.

personas.name: Coroner released, ready
personas.description: The coroner investigated, released the death with no inquest and the registrar has the coroner's certificate; no medical examiner confirmation is needed. Expect ready-to-register, clock not started, with only the coroner-released flag.

flaggedIssues.description: The coroner has released the death. Registration proceeds on the coroner’s certificate; for a cremation the coroner also sends the Cremation 6 certificate.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Book the registration appointment; the registrar will contact the informant.

personas.name: Incomplete, wrong jurisdiction and informant
personas.description: Death in Scotland, MCCD not received, medical examiner not yet confirmed, and the informant is a neighbour who does not qualify. Expect incomplete with jurisdiction, MCCD, medical-examiner and informant flags and the matching blocking rules.

blockingRules.description: The death must have occurred in England or Wales; other jurisdictions register elsewhere.
The medical certificate of cause of death has not been received.
The medical examiner has not confirmed that the death can be registered.
The informant is not a qualified informant under section 16 of the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1953.

flaggedIssues.description: The death did not occur in England or Wales. This process does not apply; Scotland, Northern Ireland and deaths abroad have their own registration rules and deadlines.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Register with the registrar for the country where the death occurred, or with the FCDO for a death abroad.

flaggedIssues.description: The medical certificate of cause of death (MCCD) has not been received by the register office.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Ask the doctor or hospital bereavement office to send the MCCD to the register office.

flaggedIssues.description: The medical examiner has not confirmed that the death can be registered, so the 5-day clock has not started.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Wait for the medical examiner’s office to contact the informant; do not book to register before then.

flaggedIssues.description: The informant is not a qualified informant. Only a relative, a person present at the death, the occupier of the premises, or the person arranging the funeral can register.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Ask a qualified informant to register the death, or check the registrar’s guidance for exceptions.

flaggedIssues.description: No registration appointment is booked.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Book an appointment with the register office for the district where the death occurred.

personas.name: Blank state
personas.description: Nothing answered. Expect incomplete: name and date of death, jurisdiction, coroner answer, MCCD, medical examiner and informant rules all fire; only the copies and appointment flags are raised.

blockingRules.description: The name of the deceased and the date of death are required.
The death must have occurred in England or Wales; other jurisdictions register elsewhere.
Whether the death was reported to a coroner has not been answered.
The medical certificate of cause of death has not been received.
The medical examiner has not confirmed that the death can be registered.
The name of the person registering the death is required.
The informant is not a qualified informant under section 16 of the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1953.

flaggedIssues.description: No registration appointment is booked.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Book an appointment with the register office for the district where the death occurred.

flaggedIssues.description: No certified copies of the death certificate are planned. Banks, insurers and probate usually each need one.
flaggedIssues.suggestedAction: Decide how many copies are needed; copies are cheaper bought at registration than ordered later.
